ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed general partners, limited partners, and each UBO at or above 25% against the UN Consolidated List, the Canadian domestic sanctions lists maintained by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the US OFAC SDN list, and applicable politically exposed persons (PEP) lists, including domestic and foreign public officials and heads of international organizations, consistent with FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons and sanctions compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Registre des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the registered name of a Quebec limited partnership must be in French, and the mandatory legal form descriptor is 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'. Names must be expressed in Latin script; ideographic or non-Latin scripts are not accepted and must be transliterated into French/Latin letters. A non-French name may be used only where a statutory exception applies, such as a recognized trademark or an established foreign name. Descriptive elements must be in French and the name must not be misleading or contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registraire refuses the proposed name, the filer may immediately file a revised devise within the initial 30-day reservation window. A written application for review must be submitted to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, stating the grounds and attaching the corrected proposed name and explanatory submissions. If the Registraire maintains the refusal, an application for judicial review may be filed before the Court of Québec in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable only as a mailing or administrative address for registry and service-of-notice purposes; it is not sufficient as the sole place where books, records, and membership/partner registers are physically kept. For an authorized economic operator (AEO) supply-chain audit profile, a genuine physical establishment in Quebec with control over records and personnel is expected. Pure virtual-office arrangements would raise commercial substance concerns and materially increase inspection risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% risk in the first 12 months if only virtual substance is maintained; the likelihood increases to approximately 65% if the entity proceeds with AEO validation and Canadian customs supply-chain audit registration, as CBSA and Quebec authorities may conduct unannounced on-site verifications.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2186-2276 (contract of partnership and limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, arts. 21-40; Regulation respecting fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Gouvernement du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Quebec limited partnership; no escrow account is prescribed by law. The partnership agreement must fix the contributions of the general and limited partners, and contributions may be made in money or property, with any real-rights contribution requiring notarial form.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the initial organizational resolution of the General Partner of [Limited Partnership Name], effective immediately, that: (1) the partnership agreement is adopted, and the capital commitment schedule is approved for subscription by partners through cash, property, or services permitted under the Civil Code of Québec; (2) the registered office is fixed at [full street address], Montréal, Province of Québec; (3) [Full Name] is appointed General Partner Representative and is authorized to execute and file the declaration of limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to complete Canada Revenue Agency registrations; and (4) any lawful ancillary actions required to formalize the partnership are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Optional Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online registry search and reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Quebec enterprise registry to verify that the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to existing legal or registered names, and compliant with Quebec naming rules under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. If the name is distinctive, submit an optional name reservation application through the Registrar's online services before the declaration of registration is filed.
required_dossiers: Proposed distinct legal name
Certificate of name reservation, if obtained
Basic identification of the filer or general partner applying for reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, file a corrected substitution request or provide written justification to the Registrar; an administrative refusal may be contested before the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal legal counsel or Québec notary; not a government filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec. The agreement must identify the general partner and limited partners, capital contributions, profit distribution, management authority, restrictions on limited-partner participation in management, registered office, and dissolution events. If any partner contributes an immovable or real right, authenticate the contribution by notarial deed. Execute all relevant resolutions and mandates before proceeding to registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or corporate extract for each partner
Draft or final limited partnership agreement
Proof of authority for any corporate general partner, including board resolution
Contact and registered-office details for the partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: This is an internal contractual step; if defects are identified, execute an amending or restated partnership agreement before filing the declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online declaration of registration for a limited partnership. Enter the legal name, Quebec registered-office address, general partner identity, limited partner information if required, object or business scope, and principal establishment address for ISIC 7020 supply-chain and customs security audit services. Attach or reference any name reservation certificate. Pay the applicable filing fee and sign electronically or, if paper filing is used, provide notarized signature where required.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration of registration for a limited partnership
Name reservation certificate, if any
Mandate or power of attorney for the filer acting on behalf of the partnership
Consent of each general partner to act as general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of refusal or query, file the corrected information or provide a legal explanation within the prescribed period; a refusal can be contested by an application to the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Quebec Enterprise Number and Registry Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — post-filing issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the declaration is accepted, verify the online registry record, record the Quebec Enterprise Number, and download official attestations or extracts. Retain the registered office address and registry information in the partnership books. Registration is the legal publicity event that preserves the liability limitation for limited partners with respect to third parties.
required_dossiers: Registry file reference or Quebec Enterprise Number
Approved declaration summary from the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry record contains errors, file a declaration of modification or rectification with the Registrar; for material refusals, appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration portal and Revenu Québec business registration services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for a partnership Business Number through the CRA Business Registration Service. If the partnership carries on taxable commercial activities in Canada, register for GST/HST; if making taxable supplies in Quebec, assess QST registration requirements with Revenu Québec. Prepare to file partnership information returns, and note that the limited partnership itself is not subject to income tax but must report to the Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec.
required_dossiers: Quebec Enterprise Number and registry attestation
Limited partnership agreement
Residential and business addresses of all partners
Description of business activities using ISIC 7020
Anticipated taxable-supply estimate for GST/HST/QST purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec requests clarification, respond through the Business Window or the applicable business registration helpline; if an account is denied or altered, provide supporting documentation or apply for ministerial relief within the applicable objection period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Books and Records Custody
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered Canadian bank, credit union, or authorized financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the completed organizational file to the financial institution and open a partnership bank account in the name of the limited partnership. Appoint the General Partner Representative as signing officer and provide beneficial ownership information to satisfy the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Deliver any capital contribution and establish accounting records, partnership minute books, and safe custody for governance documents at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Quebec registry attestation showing the Quebec Enterprise Number
CRA Business Number confirmation
Certified or original limited partnership agreement
General Partner resolution appointing the representative
Identity and beneficial-ownership documents for all partners and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution requests enhanced due diligence, supply a source-of-funds declaration, beneficial-ownership diagram, and professional references; adjust signing authority by supplementary general partner resolution if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Records and Compliance Calendar Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner management office and external legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a compliance calendar covering annual registry declarations required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, partnership information returns, GST/HST and QST filings, voluntary CBSA partner-program renewals, and audit-manual updates. Record any change of registered office, general partner, or limited partner and file declarations of modification with the Registrar within the statutory delay.
required_dossiers: Governance records binder containing the partnership agreement and resolutions
Compliance calendar template
Registry and tax account reference numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For late filings, file the outstanding declaration promptly, pay any penalty, and request cancellation or reduction of penalties based on reasonable-cause explanations filed with the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No mandatory industrial licensing board applies to ISIC 7020 professional management and supply-chain audit services; voluntary trade-security accreditation is administered by Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), Customs Security Unit, through the Partners in Protection (PIP) and Canadian CUSP program.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating licence is required for an office-based consulting and AEO security-audit practice. CBSA Partners in Protection / CUSP membership is a voluntary accreditation, not a governmental operating licence, and may be pursued as a client-facing trade-security credential.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Gouvernement du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office and professional practical services generate no industrial discharge or land disturbance, so no full EIA authorization or environmental registration is triggered. Any future leasehold fit-out is assessed under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2, and municipal building permit rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Ordinary office sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws; HVAC refrigerants and ozone-depleting substances must be handled by the landlord under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 and Quebec regulations; waste must be collected by authorized municipal or licensed private waste carriers, with no hazardous-waste generation expected from this activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a municipal fire safety inspection or certificate for the leased office under the Fire Safety Act and Building Act; obtain any required occupancy permit for the specific consulting and records-storage use. No structural-load inspection is required unless heavy audit-equipment or server installations exceed the designed floor load. If employees are hired, register the employer with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) and maintain the required workplace health and safety program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal income tax, GST/HST, and the Business Number (BN), administered online through Business Registration Online (BRO) and the My Business Account portal; concurrently, Revenu Québec administers Québec provincial income tax, the Québec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), and provincial payroll accounts under the provincial Taxation Act and the Tax Administration Act, using the 'mon dossier d'entreprise' portal and the 10-digit Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ) issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the société en commandite (Québec limited partnership) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); an extra-provincial or foreign partnership carrying on business in Québec must register within 60 days of establishing an establishment in Québec, thereby obtaining the NEQ which anchors all Revenu Québec tax accounts. Step 2: Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) and the GST/HST 'RT' program account from the CRA by applying through Business Registration Online or by completing and filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts); a non-resident partnership may alternatively use Form RC298 for GST/HST registration only, identifying the partnership as a separate person for GST purposes and naming the general partner. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec for QST under the 'RM' program account, plus employer source-deduction, QPIP, and CNESST accounts if personnel are engaged in Québec, using Revenu Québec's electronic registration service within 'mon dossier d'entreprise' or Form LM-1-V; QST registration becomes compulsory once the LP ceases to be a small supplier, while voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Step 4: Maintain program accounts by notifying CRA and Revenu Québec of changes within 30 days, including changes of place of business, general partner, or non-resident status; keep a complete technical file evidencing the LP's Canadian permanent establishment position and partnership registration for treaty and customs purposes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) exercises monetary authority and operates the national large-value settlement system; prudential banking regulation is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); transaction-level anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing supervision is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); Quebec-specific money-services business registration is supervised by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Canada does not operate a dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration because the Canadian dollar is governed under a non-restricted, free-float legal regime that is not subject to exchange-control permits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account bases. There are no exchange-control licences, no prior Central Bank authorizations, and no statutory hurdles for inward/outbound wire transfers, equity injections, partnership capital contributions, profit distributions, or foreign consulting-fee repatriation. Profit-remittance friction is exclusively tax-driven: for a Quebec limited partnership, a non-resident limited or general partner's allocable share of Canadian-source business income is reportable on NR4-T4A and distributions to that partner are subject to Income Tax Act (ITA) Part XIII withholding (statutory 25%, reducible under an applicable tax treaty via Form NR7/NR301). For the AEO supply-chain audit consultancy, exported management-consulting services are generally zero-rated for GST/QST (Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, section 7 and the Quebec QST equivalent) when the recipient is non-resident and the services relate to property outside Canada. No additional convertibility tax, remittance levy, or IOF-style charge applies in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory repatriation, or conversion-ratio rules exist under Canadian federal or Quebec law. Formal foreign-exchange controls were abolished in 1951. The LP may retain USD, EUR, or other foreign-currency receivables from AEO audit services indefinitely, either offshore or in a domestic foreign-currency account at a Schedule I chartered bank; the surrender ratio is 0% and there is no statutory timeline for conversion. The only mandatory obligations are: (i) FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting (EFTR) by the financial institution for each international wire of CAD 10,000 or more or its foreign-currency equivalent; (ii) conversion of foreign-currency income into Canadian dollars at the Bank of Canada daily rate for income-tax computation under ITA subsection 261(1); and (iii) standard anti-money-laundering documentation required at account establishment. No approval from the Bank of Canada or the Department of Finance is required to repatriate proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: MEDIUM, constrained. Wise Inc. (Wise Payments Ltd.) is registered with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business in Canada and must satisfy Quebec AMF licensing under the Act respecting money-services businesses (M-30.1) if it maintains an establishment in Quebec. Wise is legally usable by the Quebec LP as a supplementary low-value collection/disbursement rail (matching target payment rail 'Wise'), but it cannot replace a Schedule I chartered-bank relationship: it offers no escrow, no commercial letter of credit, no Canada Revenue Agency payroll source-deduction clearing, no LVTS access, and no institutional-grade settlement status. Tier-1 banks treat Wise transfers as third-party settlements and will require full reconciliation. Permissible use is limited to transactions below CAD 5,000 per item, each labelled with an invoice reference, with end-of-day sweeping to the primary bank account. Comparable EMIs (OFX, Vault, Airwallex) face the same Quebec licensing constraint and lower onboarding acceptance. If Wise does not hold a valid AMF Quebec endorsement, its viability drops to LOW and should be replaced with bank FX rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or supervised live-video presence of a General Partner representative is effectively mandatory; fully remote opening with no live interview is not available for a newly registered pass-through limited partnership with non-resident limited partners. Under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance, each schedule I bank must identify the LP and all beneficial owners holding at least 25% of the partnership, including the ultimate natural persons of the corporate General Partner. Quebec Tier-1 practice requires an in-branch fit-and-proper interview at a Montreal or Quebec City corporate banking centre, with passport and proof-of-address, online verification of the Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation d'immatriculation, and certified execution of the partnership agreement and GP resolution. National Bank and BMO will accept a live interactive video KYC session where a relationship manager participates and the file is low-risk, but non-resident partners still require identity verification through notarized or apostilled foreign documents. Engagement of a Quebec CPAA (Comptables professionnels agréés/CPA) sponsor materially accelerates the interview and decision process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered limited-partnership ownership with opaque foreign limited partners, triggering beneficial-ownership and source-of-control red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement (contrat de société); Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation d'immatriculation dated within 30 days; full beneficial-ownership schedule cascading every partner to natural-person level with percentage interests; organizational chart of the corporate General Partner; certified passports and proof-of-address for all 25%+ beneficial owners; six-month bank statements of principal partners; CRA business number and partnership registration number; GP resolution appointing the designated Quebec signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident capital injection from a low-tax or non-treaty jurisdiction creating source-of-funds and round-tripping suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement and capital-account ledger; incoming wire message quoting 'Partner Capital Contribution'; twelve-month source-of-funds bank statements of the remitting partner; tax-residency certificate (CRA NR303 or competent-authority certificate); sworn source-of-wealth declaration (sale of business, salary, inheritance); the LP's most recent compiled or audited financial statements; a written Part XIII withholding analysis (NR4-T4A schedules) showing how future distributions will be taxed; Canadian legal opinion confirming non-residence and absence of tax-avoidance purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border consultancy receipts with minimal documentation, raising manufactured-invoice or money-laundering-substitute flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed AEO certification and supply-chain audit retainer agreements with clients; itemized invoices linked to deliverable milestones; CRA T5013 partnership income schedules for the prior two years; engagement letters from a Quebec CPA firm; corporate substance exhibits (office lease, payroll, operational website, LinkedIn activity); an internal AML compliance manual designating a compliance officer; bank transaction statistics matching declared client descriptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) exposure arising from logistics, customs, or security-sector clientele
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-name screening certificates covering Global Affairs Canada, OFAC/OFSI, UNSC, EU, and DFATD lists; corporate registry extracts showing ultimate beneficial owners of clients; the LP's internal sanctions and anti-bribery policy; AEO accreditation evidence (C-TPAT, AEO-EU) demonstrating operation within regulated customs frameworks; signed declaration of no beneficial interest in sensitive jurisdictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Registration (Déclaration annuelle) for a Quebec limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary date of the entity's initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 120 per occurrence; repeated default for five consecutive years can result in administrative radiation from the registry, and unregistered documents lose enforceability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and Quebec Partnership Income Tax Information Return (T5013 Summary and Relevé 15 / RL-15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: T5013 must be filed within five months after the partnership fiscal period end; Relevé 15 / RL-15 in respect of limited partners must be provided by the applicable provincial return-filing deadline (generally February 28 or March 31 of the following calendar year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty starts at CAD 100 per month per partner, capped per partner account; Quebec penalties apply under the Taxation Act for overdue RL-15 forms, and interest accrues on any unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return and Quebec QST Return (where the limited partnership is a registrant)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Federal GST/HST) and Revenu Québec (QST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, no later than three months after the fiscal year end of the partnership; for certain non-resident registrants, the deadline is legible on the CRA/Revenu Québec notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; Quebec QST late filing penalties are assessed separately under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Quebec statutory audit threshold applies specifically to a limited partnership merely because of its legal form; an audit may become compulsory under the partnership agreement, by a lender or other contractual covenant, or if the entity qualifies as an investment fund or reporting issuer under securities legislation. A management consultancy LP will generally have no statutory audit unless such a requirement is imposed by third-party agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is the default for a private limited partnership with no public accountability; IFRS as issued by the IASB becomes mandatory if the partnership is listed or designated as a publicly accountable enterprise. The partnership tracks income under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act on a fiscal-period basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's Transparency in Enterprises Act (Loi concernant la transparence en matière d'entreprises) requires enterprises registered with the Registraire des entreprises to identify their main beneficiaries, including general partners and any limited partners holding 25% or more of capital or control rights, and this information must be confirmed in the annual declaration under the phased implementation schedule. Internally, the general partner must approve and document any change in partner identities, capital contributions, or profit-sharing rights at the annual partner meeting; for Canadian anti-money-laundering compliance, a KYC review identifying and confirming beneficial ownership must be conducted at least annually if the LP acts as a reporting entity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–15,000 per annum for a certified audit; USD 2,500–6,000 per annum for a review engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate rate (15% federal Part I + 11.5% Quebec provincial rate); the Canada Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and no entity-level income tax is imposed on the partnership itself.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays for the LP. Preferential measures generally available to partners include federal SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable for Canadian-controlled private corporations and 15% non-refundable for others), Quebec research and development tax credits up to 30% for eligible corporations, and the reduced small business rate for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations. These incentives apply at the partner level because of the LP's flow-through classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal Form T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary; electronically filed through CRA-approved tax preparation software or the CRA's T5013 Internet Filing and EFILE system; the partnership must first register for a CRA business number (BN).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, for each partnership fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 return must be filed within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, the due date is May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA-assigned nine-digit business number for the limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partnerships carrying on business in Canada must obtain a Canadian business number before filing; include the operating name and the Canadian agent appointed for service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date on which the partnership's fiscal period ends, entered as YYYY-MM-DD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal period established in the partnership agreement and reported to the CRA; non-resident partners may not substitute a home-country fiscal year for Canadian reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross business revenue from AEO certification auditing and supply-chain security consulting services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue; services physically performed outside Canada and without a Canadian permanent establishment are not subject to Part I tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share of net income or loss allocated to each partner according to the partnership agreement, cross-referenced to T5013 Schedule 50.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident partners, their country of residence, and any treaty claim; do not withhold Part XIII tax on business income where the non-resident is taxable under Part I through a permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013 may result in a penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500 per partnership return under section 162(7) of the Income Tax Act; knowing or grossly negligent false statements attract a 50% civil penalty on the understated tax and may trigger criminal prosecution under section 239.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec Form CO-1029, Déclaration complémentaire des sociétés de personnes, and associated Relevé 15 schedules; filed electronically through Revenu Québec's Mon Dossier and E-services portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, the due date is June 30 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec establishment number, legal name, and registered address of the limited partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partnership carrying on business in Quebec must appoint an agent for service of process in Quebec and include the agent's contact details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net amount of revenue and expenses attributable to the Quebec business of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Quebec-source revenue; management consultancy services physically rendered outside Quebec are generally not allocable to Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage of income or loss distributed to each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report each non-resident partner's percentage, residence jurisdiction, and whether the partner carries on business in Quebec through a permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec assesses late-filing penalties of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500, plus administrative service fees; failure to remit Quebec source deductions or QST creates additional civil penalties and director-liability exposure in the case of a corporate general partner.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends and deemed dividends paid or credited to non-residents of Canada. For a Canadian limited partnership, current distributions are not generally treated as dividends; rather, non-resident partners are taxed on their allocable share of Canadian-source business income under Part I unless relieved by an applicable tax treaty. A treaty may reduce the statutory withholding rate to 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on shareholding level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident partner must obtain a certificate of residence from the home-country competent authority and deliver Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty for a Reduced Rate of Non-Resident Tax Withholding) to the Canadian withholding agent or to the CRA. The withholding agent must remit at the reduced rate only after receiving the completed form; if the full 25% is withheld, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the CRA within two years from the end of the calendar year in which the amount was withheld, ordinarily using Form T112. Revenu Québec follows the same federal treaty determination for Quebec tax purposes under the Canada-Quebec tax collection agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rate is 25% for royalty payments and certain interest payments to non-residents. Arm's-length interest paid to non-residents is generally exempt from Canadian withholding unless the recipient is a foreign related party or the interest is participating debt. Under most Canadian income tax treaties, royalty withholding is reduced to 0%, 5%, or 10%, and interest to 10% or 15%, subject to beneficial-ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Income Tax Act imposes no explicit statutory monetary threshold for contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation; however, CRA administrative practice requires documentation for all non-arm's length cross-border transactions and focuses review on specified transactions exceeding CAD 5 million annually. Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenue of CAD 750 million or more, and such groups must also maintain OECD-aligned Master File and Local File documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. The applicable substance doctrine is the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under section 245 of the Income Tax Act, which denies a tax benefit arising from an avoidance transaction lacking genuine economic substance or a bona fide business purpose. Revenu Québec applies a parallel anti-avoidance rule in section 315 of the Quebec Taxation Act. For partnerships, the CRA and courts will also consider whether the LP has a real commercial presence, active management, and an actual risk-bearing role in the supply-chain consulting services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Unreported Canadian-Source Partnership Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident limited partner or the corporate general partner intentionally omits the partner's allocable share of income from the T5013, misstates the partner's country of residence, or fails to file a non-resident Part I tax return despite carrying on business in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239(1): on summary conviction, a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, a fine of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2) of 50% of the understated tax, plus interest on arrears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner who knew or consented to the omission are jointly and severally liable under section 227.1 of the Income Tax Act for unremitted source deductions; the Canada Border Services Agency may issue a departure order or travel ban where tax debt exceeds CAD 10,000; directors may also face criminal proceedings as parties to the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing - Arm's-Length and Documentation Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The limited partnership charges a non-resident affiliate a non-arm's length fee for AEO audit services without a functional and risk analysis, fails to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation, or uses an unsubstantiated cost-plus margin inconsistent with independent market benchmarks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 247(2) permits the CRA to redetermine the arm's-length amount; section 247(3) imposes a penalty equal to 10% of the gross transfer-pricing adjustment if the taxpayer did not make reasonable efforts and did not maintain contemporaneous documentation. Reassessment interest compounds daily, and Quebec may assess a parallel provincial penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the pricing without genuine reliance on professional advice may be held civilly liable for the resulting corporate penalty and interest; the CRA may assert transferee liability under section 160 where assets were transferred to a director at less than fair market value.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and General Anti-Avoidance Rule Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LP is used as a conduit or a paper entity with no employees, no office, no Canadian decision-making, and no real supply-chain audit activities, artificially routing revenue to a non-resident affiliate to avoid Canadian Part I tax, GST/HST, and permanent-establishment exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment denies the tax benefit and re-characterizes the transaction under section 245; false statements in the T5013 attract a 50% gross-negligence penalty under section 163(2); failure to report foreign-related transactions or treaty-based positions may trigger additional penalties of CAD 2,500 plus CAD 25 per day for non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a sole corporate general partner may be assessed personally as transferees, as trustees for unpaid partnership tax liabilities, or as participants in a fraudulent disposition; Canadian courts may pierce the corporate veil in cases of sham, agency, or over-controlling management by a corporate partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs and AEO Supply-Chain Security Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LP, acting as an AEO certification and supply-chain security auditor, knowingly certifies a client's compliance file despite material false declarations, missing container security documentation, invalid business numbers, or undisclosed customs non-compliance, thereby facilitating a customs fraud scheme.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs Act section 109.1 provides monetary penalties of CAD 10,000 to CAD 100,000 for making false statements to the Canada Border Services Agency; AEO authorization may be suspended or revoked; Criminal Code section 380, fraud over CAD 5,000, is punishable by up to 14 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally direct or approve the false certification may be charged as parties to the offence under the Criminal Code; the CBSA may issue administrative penalties directly against a professional adviser, and professional-liability claims from clients may strip corporate veil where the director provided personal guarantees or exercised day-to-day control.
